title: MIXED METALS AND CONSTRUCTION DEBRIS SCRAP REMOVAL TERM CONTRACT � ANNISTON ARMY DEPOT (ANAD)
description: MIXED METALS AND CONSTRUCTION DEBRIS SCRAP REMOVAL TERM CONTRACT � ANNISTON ARMY DEPOT (ANAD) IFB Number: 2-1-QSC-T-27-008 Location: Anniston Army Depot, Anniston, Alabama The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) is soliciting sealed bids for the recurring purchase and removal of Government-owned Demilitarization Code A (DEMIL A) Mixed Metals Scrap generated at Anniston Army Depot (ANAD). PROPERTY DESCRIPTION Scrap may include ferrous and non-ferrous metals, construction and demolition scrap metal, structural steel, milling machines, lathes, air-conditioning units, motorized equipment, manufacturing machinery, equipment components, and other designated DEMIL A scrap materials. Army Working Capital Fund (AWCF) scrap is excluded. ESTIMATED ANNUAL QUANTITY Approximately 1,000,000 pounds (446.43 gross tons). Quantities, composition, frequency, and availability are estimates only and are not guaranteed. CONTRACT TERM One (1) year base period with four (4) one-year Government option periods, for a maximum potential term of five (5) years. BID PRICING Bidders shall offer a percentage of the Fastmarkets MB-STE-0788 Steel Scrap Shredder Feed, FOB Southeast, $/gross ton market index. All bids must be expressed as percentages to no more than two (2) decimal places. CONTRACTOR REQUIREMENTS The awarded Contractor shall furnish and maintain five (5) heavy-duty 20-yard roll-off containers and five (5) heavy-duty 30-yard roll-off containers. The Contractor is responsible for providing transportation, labor, equipment, and necessary removal services in accordance with the IFB. description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of Information and Technology (OIT), Product Delivery Services (PDS), Data, Artificial Intelligence, and Innovation Services (DAIS) Portfolio has a requirement for brand name Cockroach Database (CRDB) Subscription Licenses and Maintenance, inclusive of software updates, fixes, security alerts, patches, and 24/7 customer support, herein referred to as software support. VA's existing Summit Data Platform (SDP) requires CRDB, a cloud-native database supporting multi-cloud and hybrid deployments across diverse environments. The SDP requires a database solution that ensures high elasticity and consistency to support mission-critical workloads. This solution must adhere to ACID (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) principles, ensuring reliable data transactions across multiple environments. The database must be deployable across various physical nodes and cloud regions, offering flexibility in scaling operations. The solution must also include non-intrusive, near real-time Change Data Capture (CDC) capabilities, enabling seamless data updates to the SDP. The solution must support multi-cloud hybrid deployments, allowing integration across Data Centers, On-Premise, VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC), GovCloud, and Microsoft Azure Government (MAG) environments. Geo-partitioning is required to optimize latency and ensure consistent and responsive performance for VA operations nationwide. The solution must also provide resilience and elastic scaling to handle machines, datacenter, and regional failures, maintaining continuous operation without manual intervention. Together, these capabilities enable VA to accurately capture operational data and deliver near real-time insight and analytics, ensuring decision makers and customer service staff have accurate, current information to better serve Veterans. The Contractor shall provide up to 300 hours of incidental services support within the 12-month licensing period. description: Los Servicios Científico-Técnicos (SCT) de la UIB disponen únicamente de un equipo de GC-MS de cuadrupolo adquirido el año 2005, el cual ha presentado problemas de conectividad y de adquisición de cromatogramas durante los últimos meses, llegando a estar largos períodos averiado, con el consiguiente perjuicio de los usuarios y el desarrollo de sus proyectos de investigación. Debido su antigüedad resulta muy complicado conseguir algunas piezas de recambio para su reparación. Además, el analizador del GC ha quedado obsoleto y no permite la ejecución de análisis MS/MS ni métodos de cribado ni métodos no-dirigidos. El objetivo de este contrato es adquirir un analizador de alta resolución (Q/TOF u Orbitrap) acoplado a GC que permita desarrollar tanto métodos de identificación como cuantificación, en análisis dirigidos, de sospechosos y no-dirigidos mediante MS/MS, con mejor sensibilidad que el analizador disponible en la actualidad. Por ello, en estos momentos, los SCT no son capaces de ofrecer un servicio adecuado acorde a las necesidades de sus usuarios, al no disponer de ningún equipamiento funcional de GC-MS para la determinación cualitativa y cuantitativa de compuestos orgánicos volátiles y semivolátiles en muestras de origen ambiental, biológico, alimentario e industrial presentadas en los diferentes estados de agregación de la materia. El objeto del contrato coincide con el equipo financiado por la Agencia Estatal de Investigación en la ayuda EQC2025-009163.

description: The Los Angeles District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is seeking to lease a minimum of 1,381 net/usable to a maximum of 1,874 gross/rentable square feet (gross square feet to include any common area factor), of existing Class A or B retail space, in Delano, CA, within the defined Delineated area (DA) boundaries below: North -- South -- East � West � The Government�s desire is for a full-service lease of Retail space for an Armed Forces Career Center for a term not to exceed five (5) years with Government termination rights. Interested respondents may include building owners and representatives with the exclusive right to represent building owners. Additional lighted parking must be available during business hours, weekends and holidays, for approximately 5 employee vehicles and visitors/recruit candidate parking. Must use the Government Lease. The military services shall have the right to use space beyond normal working hours and, if required, on Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays. This includes the use of elevators, lights, toilet facilities, and, if necessary, heating and air conditioning. Special attention should be given to security requirements (video entry control system, closed circuit television system and video recording, dual roller shades on exterior windows, fixed panel shade on exterior entry door and peep hole in secondary exit, perforated window wrap), fragmentation film on exterior windows/glass doors, telecommunication wiring requirements, addition of water fountain, signage, paint, wall graphics, phone jacks, electrical outlets, and spec'd carpet squares. These are items that can add a significant cost and may be overlooked in the bid process; however, all items in the specifications need to be followed, even if code does not require the item (i.e., smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, etc.). Bids shall include any tear down/haul away expenses. Submitted floor plans must meet the space requirements as designated on attached example. title: Request for Information (RFI) for Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Protection (JPM CBRN P) Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS)
description: This is a request for information (RFI) only for capabilities and experience which show potential for meeting the requirements described below. This is not a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP) or an Invitation for Bid (IFB). It is a market research tool being used to determine the availability and adequacy of potential sources for planning purposes only. Responses to this notice are not considered as offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of responses nor otherwise pay for the preparation of any information presented or the use of any such information. 1. Purpose The Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Protection (JPM CBRN P) is conducting a market survey to identify industry capabilities, experience, and potential approaches for serving as a Product Support Integrator (PSI) and material integration support for the Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS) Reconfiguration and Technology Refresh effort. The Government seeks a commercial partner capable of procuring and coordinating the delivery of commercially available components; receiving, tracking, and consolidating Government-sourced components; applying Item Unique Identification (IUID) markings as required; maintaining materiel accountability and readiness; conducting Preventative Maintenance, Checks and Services (PMCS) and Care of Supply in Storage (COSIS) as necessary, and delivering verified, complete component packages to Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA) for final system integration, build completion, and packaging. This RFI is issued solely for planning and market-research purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, commitment by the Government, or authorization to incur costs. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. 2. Background CP DEPMEDS is a fielded CBRN protection system that supports Army Role 3 field-hospital operations. The program is executing a reconfiguration and technology-refresh effort using fielded, previously qualified, and commercially available components. The revised support concept under consideration would use a commercial PSI to integrate component procurement, Government-furnished or Government-sourced materiel coordination, traceability, IUID marking, and delivery to Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA). PBA would retain responsibility for final assembly/integration of CP DEPMEDS sets, final packaging, associated Government acceptance activities, and delivery of sets to their fielding/final destination. 3. Scope of Information Requested The Government seeks information on industry capability to perform the following functions: A. Commercial Component Procurement Procure commercially available components identified by the Government. Conduct vendor management and order placement of components. Identify long-lead items, supply-chain constraints, discontinuance risks, and proposed alternate sources. Provide proposed substitutes only when specifically authorized by the Government. Manage warranties, vendor documentation, certificates of conformance, and commercial shipping documentation as applicable. B. Government Component Coordination Coordinate receipt, transfer, and consolidation of Government-sourced components from designated Government organizations, depots, supply activities, or other locations. Maintain accountability for Government-provided or Government-directed materiel while in contractor custody. Maintain COSIS to prevent environmental degradation, corrosion, and shelf life expiration of stored equipment and supplies. Reconcile shipping discrepancies, damaged materiel, shortages, overages, and documentation issues. Maintain traceability between each component, its source, and its assigned CP DEPMEDS configuration or set. Note: The contractor would not independently obligate Government funds or direct Government supply activities. The Government would retain authority for requisitions, funding, release, acceptance, and disposition decisions. C. IUID and Asset Identification Apply, validate, and document IUID markings for designated end items and components in accordance with Government-furnished requirements and applicable standards. Verify marking quality, placement, readability, and association with the correct item record. Maintain item-level records linking serial number, part number, National Stock Number, Unique Item Identifier, source, and destination. Provide electronic IUID and asset-accountability data deliverables in a Government-specified format. D. Materiel Receiving, Inspection, and Staging Receive and inspect commercial and Government-sourced components. Verify quantities, part numbers, serial numbers, condition, shelf life, and required documentation. Store and stage components in a manner that preserves condition, supports shelf-life management, and enables rapid consolidation into required delivery packages. Maintain COSIS to prevent environmental degradation, corrosion, and shelf life expiration of stored equipment and supplies. E. Kit Completion and Delivery to PBA Build component-level shipping packages in accordance with Government-approved bills of material, configuration lists, and delivery priorities. Conduct kit-completeness checks before shipment. Package, preserve, mark, and ship components to PBA in accordance with Government-approved shipping instructions. Provide advance-shipment notifications, packing lists, serial-number/IUID records, and discrepancy reports. If required, travel to PBA to help support the delivery and inventory of shipped equipment. F. Program Management and Reporting Maintain an integrated procurement and delivery schedule. Provide recurring status reports addressing procurement status, component availability, shortages, long-lead risks, delivery forecasts, IUID status, kit completion, and shipment status. Identify risks early and recommend mitigation actions, including alternate vendors, phased deliveries, or proposed substitutes. Participate in Government-led integrated product team meetings as required. 4. Desired Capabilities Respondents should describe experience performing comparable work involving: Multi-vendor procurement and materiel integration; Government-furnished property or Government-directed materiel; IUID marking, validation, and data management; Military logistics, asset accountability, and shipping documentation; Kitting, staging, packaging, preservation, and shipment of complex equipment; Supply-chain risk management and long-lead-item mitigation; CBRN, deployable medical, field-hospital, shelter, or comparable expeditionary equipment. (Note: This is desired experience but not required for response.) The Government is particularly interested in respondents able to manage multiple sources of supply and coordinate delivery of components to a Government integration location. 5. Industry Response Instructions Responses should not exceed [15] pages, excluding attachments. Include: Company Information: Name, UEI, CAGE code, business size, socioeconomic status, and points of contact. Relevant Experience: Up to three relevant efforts performed within the past five years. Technical Approach: Notional approach to commercial procurement, Government-component coordination, IUID, accountability, staging, kit verification, and delivery to PBA. Facilities and Workforce: Relevant facilities, quality systems, logistics staff, IUID capability, and geographic support model. Data and Reporting: Proposed methods for inventory visibility, serialized-item traceability, IUID data delivery, and Government status reporting.
